entry.runs: desktop SessionHostTransport.invokeControlResult -> standalone session-service.mjs createSessionService -> session-runtime/resource-api.mjs createResourceApi (the sign-in registry is real); the MCP client is fake

product.tree: product tree loaded by the recorder

replay.compare: mixdog-app-server / mixdog-mcp: the sign-in flow keeps its pending/complete state across control-session replacement; compare each result with the flow id and session ids abstracted
replay.entry: mixdog-mcp McpService (DomainService::call) mcp/signOutMcpServer, mcp/beginMcpOAuthLogin, mcp/mcpStatus, mcp/getMcpOAuthLoginStatus, mcp/completeMcpOAuthLogin over the real sign-in registry (mcp_logins.rs McpLogins, as mcp_glue.rs begin_login/login_status/complete_login reach it); the MCP client is the recording's fake (LoginBackend/LoginSession: the recorded authorize URL, the recorded callback, the recorded refusal of another paste).

normalised.flowId: generated by the sign-in registry; written <flow> wherever it occurs (paths listed in normalised.paths)
normalised.controlEnvelope: each recorded answer is the desktop control session's envelope ({value, snapshot, result: {value, sessionId, revision, full}}); the core has no control session, so each answer's value is compared whole
normalised.controlSession: controlSessionReplaced, runtimesAfterFailedRead and runtimesAfterInvalidPaste count the desktop's control-session runtimes; the core's sign-in registry is the process's own and is not replaced, which is what the case asserts: every later answer finds the same flow
